svg.text: <tspan x="588" y="216">Japan is an island country in East Asia, located in the</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="236">Pacific Ocean. It comprises an archipelago of nearly</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="256">7,000 islands, with the four largest — Honshū,</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="276">Hokkaidō, Kyūshū, and Shikoku — accounting for</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="296">about 97% of the total land area.</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="324">The nation has a population of approximately 124</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="344">million people, making it the eleventh most populous</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="364">country in the world. Tokyo, the capital, is the largest</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="384">metropolitan area globally, with over 37 million</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="404">residents.</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="432">Known for its rich cultural heritage, technological</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="452">innovation, and culinary traditions, Japan is the</tspan> <tspan x="588" y="472">world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP.</tspan>

<tspan x="70" y="618">Japan's economy, the world's fourth-largest by nominal GDP, is driven by advanced manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and services sectors.</tspan> <tspan x="70" y="638">Despite facing demographic challenges including a shrinking and aging population, Japan remains a global leader in innovation, patent filings, and</tspan> <tspan x="70" y="658">high-tech industries. The country's post-war economic miracle transformed it from a war-torn nation into an economic powerhouse, and it continues to</tspan>

<tspan x="78" y="786">Japan's nominal GDP in current US</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="806">dollars has shown relative stability over</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="826">the past decade, hovering around the</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="846">$4–5 trillion mark. After peaking near</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="866">$5.12 trillion in 2019, the economy</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="886">experienced a notable decline in 2022–</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="906">2024, largely attributed to the yen's</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="926">depreciation against the US dollar.</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="956">In real terms, Japan's domestic economy</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="976">has shown more modest but steady</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="996">growth. The nominal dollar figures are</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="1016">significantly affected by exchange rate</tspan> <tspan x="78" y="1036">fluctuations, masking underlying growth.</tspan>
